limits: Reference list is not in the PDF excerpt: footnote numbers 1-10 have no titles.
Author could not check the watermelon study's leave-one-out claim without its data.
Observational data cannot rule out unmeasured confounders; only randomisation does.
Year of publication not printed in the excerpt.
practices: Remember that a statistically insignificant variable does not necessarily have zero effect; power may be too low to detect it (Tips, p.88).
Avoid stepwise regression; the final model is biased and hard to interpret. Consider the lasso or no variable selection (Tips; p.83-84).
Check model fit on a separate dataset or with cross-validation such as leave-one-out (p.83, Tips).
Watch for confounders and Simpson's paradox; use random assignment where possible (p.87-88).
Do not read a coefficient as the effect of intervening on that variable, since variables are rarely changeable with all others held constant (p.85).
Include measured confounders (e.g. budget in class-size study) in the regression to control for them (p.80).
